To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bone diagenesis in the Greek sites is characterized by a subtle but systematic change in the unit cell parameters, as well as in the coherence length of the crystallites, that can be predicted from the infrared spectra.

bone diagenesis is accompanied by a systematic decrease of the apatite unit cell volume and coherence length and by the substitution of CO 3 3− by F − and H 2 O in the structure, which can be detected by infrared spectroscopy.

the infrared spectra of fossil bones can be used to predict their diagenetic state, which in turn can be predicted on their structural state (unit cell volume, coherence length), which in turn can all be accounted for by subtle structural changes of the carbonate ion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and vibrational characterization of bone diagenetic trends.
a detailed analysis of the vibrational and structural changes occurring in bone during diagenesis, and with a better understanding of their origin.
the identification of diagenetic processes in bone, as well as the development of a predictive tool for the assessment of the degree of diagenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diagenesis in bone is a process that involves a combination of surface and bulk modifications, which can be followed and quantified by infrared spectroscopic techniques.
diagenetic changes are primarily reflected by the infrared spectra of bone samples and are related to the structural changes in the apatite unit cell.
bone diagenesis can be characterized by the following sequence: 1) the loss of H 2 O; 2) the loss of CO 3 3− and the appearance of a distorted CO3 2− ; and 3) the substitution of OH by F −.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diagenesis is a subtle, yet systematic process that can be identified by infrared spectroscopic techniques, and that the changes in structure can be correlated to the infrared data.
the diagenetic trends in bone are not only reflected in the unit cell volume but also in the coherence length and in the vibrational properties of the CO 3  and H 2 O groups.
bone diagenesis can be characterized by a systematic decrease of the c-axis coherence length, and an increase of the unit cell parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
infrared spectroscopy can be used to identify the vibrational signatures of diagenetic processes and to quantify the degree of diagenesis in bone samples, in a non-destructive way.

infrared spectroscopy is a powerful and sensitive tool for the study of bone mineral diagenesis, and that it can complement and even replace XRD in the characterization of fossil bones, as it provides complementary information on the structural state of the apatite.

infrared spectroscopy, in combination with chemometric modelling, can provide a non-destructive and rapid means for the characterization of the diagenetic state of fossil bones, and thus contribute to the study of their palaeobiology.
